doc.title: Michael Max Fleming interviewed by Monk Rowe, New Hartford, New York, June 8, 2017

title: Advice to leave Cincinnati and play R&B bands first
summary: Visiting musicians told him not to get stuck in Cincinnati. A substitute teacher told him to learn his instrument, play R&B bands, then move to New York. He could not recall the names of the local R&B bands he played with.

story.theme_name: Coming to New York: clubs, jams, and making it
story.community_name: Making it in New York: arrival, clubs and the scene

blocks.x: That’s good. Okay so did people tell you, “You’ve got to move on. You’ve got to go to New York” did you hear that?

That’s so good. There’s two ways I heard it. Every musician, some of who worked in Las Vegas, some of whom worked with what they call carnivals traveling around. They always said, see we have a saying about — Cincinnati is a good place to be from. Which is true. So a lot of the musicians when they came through and they saw it was a young guy, would say, “Don’t get stuck here. Get out of here. Don’t get stuck.” Like that. And then there was a school teacher who was frustrated and he was a jazz musician and he couldn’t get a job in the Cincinnati school system but he was a substitute at our school. And just like I asked Coleman Hawkins, I always sought counsel. You know. I said, “Do you have a formula, what should I do. I want to go to New York and be a jazz musician. What do you think I should do?” He was trombone player which is not an easy instrument to make a living off of in the jazz world. So he says, “Well number one, go to school or whatever, go and learn to get around your instrument.” Very simple. That’s the terminology. Learn to get around your instrument. “Number two, go on the road, play with rhythm & blues bands, play with whoever you want to play with. Get experience. Then you move to New York and find your way.” So that’s what I did.
What were some of the — did you play with rhythm and blues bands and swing bands?
Yeah but they were right there. They were right there. Well I was doing it with “Cleanhead” and then Scott. What was his name. The organ player that played.

No, no, this is a saxophone player. He was a genius. And I’m having trouble remembering names but yea, the answer is I played with, I can’t think of their names but there were a lot of local rhythm & blues bands that I played with. The main thing what he was saying is get experience playing. So I did that. And yeah, so I did that, and then I went on. You were asking me if I played with the bands and I’m saying yeah, even though I can’t — so I’m just trying to think, but they don’t come to mind. Okay but go on to the next —
Okay, so did you save up some money before you went to New York? See I never did that.
And I’m not going to tell you how much now.
